question_text: Find the equation of the plane passing through (2, 3, 4) and perpendicular to the x-axis.

mark_split.label: Take the X-axis as the normal

steps.label: Take the X-axis as the normal
steps.margin_note: First mark. A plane perpendicular to a line has that line as its normal, so the X-axis itself is the normal here and its direction ratios are (1, 0, 0).
steps.memory_tip: Perpendicular to the X-axis means the X-axis IS the normal, with direction ratios (1, 0, 0).

steps.why: The normal of a plane is the direction that is perpendicular to every line in it, so saying the plane is perpendicular to the X-axis is the same as saying the X-axis points along the normal.
common_mistakes: Taking (1, 0, 0) as a line lying in the plane instead of the normal.
Writing the direction ratios of the Y-axis or the Z-axis by mistake.

steps.label: Write and simplify the plane
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Two of the three coefficients are 0, so the y and z brackets become zero and only the x coordinate of the point is left.
steps.memory_tip: b and c are 0, so the y and z terms become zero and only x = 2 is left.

steps.why: The answer keeps only the x coordinate of the given point, because moving in the y or z direction does not change which plane a point is on when the normal points along the X-axis. This plane is also parallel to the YZ-plane.
common_mistakes: Using the y or z coordinate and writing y = 3 or z = 4.
Writing x = 0, which is the YZ-plane and does not pass through the given point.
